creature fills the frame, drawn at 1.6 x 1.6 scale proportions
request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite, the zisska, a low plated stone-eating grazer, on a transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline. The body is a low, very wide flat shield about three times as wide as it is tall, spreading across the ground with its scalloped plated rim nearly touching the surface; the short legs are mostly hidden beneath the plated edge. Each plate is rough, matte, grey-brown stone with a granular, pitted surface and several concentric mineral rings like a cut agate or geode. Bright sulphur-yellow mineral crust builds up in the plate seams and rings and coats the snout plate and the mouth. The head is carried nose-down against the ground and ends in a broad, flat rasping snout plate built for scraping rock, its mouth rimmed with yellow mineral. The silhouette is a flat, wide stone disc pressed to the ground with a broad scraper snout at the front. Seen from above at a slight angle so the whole spread of the plated back shows. Even soft lighting, the creature centred and filling the frame, no ground, no shadow plane, nothing else in the image.
